answer: Sybil resistance comes from making identity cost capital: every agent locks a bond before it may attest or vote, and that bond is slashed in full if the agent is caught forging identities. Each fake agent needs its own separate bond, so an attacker's cost grows linearly with the number of identities, while an honest agent risks only one stake. Whether the trade is a pigment shipment, a relic auction, or an oasis dataset, the same deposit applies, keeping influence proportional to capital at risk, not to the keys one can generate.
